key_insight: Not every agent failure is a useful lesson. GEPA-Curator argues that self-improving agents should learn from curated tasks rather than treating all failed runs as equally informative.
problem_solved: Reflective prompt optimization can mistake harness limitations, random execution failures, or unreliable judging for prompt weaknesses, creating misleading or harmful learning signals.
method: Build on reflective prompt optimization approaches such as GEPA, which use failed agent runs to guide improvements.
Curate the tasks used for learning to prioritize useful feedback over potentially misleading failures.
The provided abstract is truncated, so the exact curation procedure and evaluation results are not available.
impact: For practitioners, this highlights the importance of feedback quality—not just collecting more failures—when improving agents. Curated learning could reduce misguided prompt updates, although the provided excerpt does not establish measured gains.
visual_elements: A failure-source diagram: prompt weakness, harness limitation, execution randomness, and judge noise.

paper_title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
